title: Schurger, Sitt, and Dehaene's alternative to the Libet reading
summary: Their 2012 PNAS paper models the readiness potential as a stochastic accumulation, not a pre-conscious decision.
body: Aaron Schurger, Jacobo D. Sitt, and Stanislas Dehaene, "An accumulator model for spontaneous neural activity prior to self-initiated movement" (PNAS, 2012), argue that the slow buildup Libet measured can arise from noisy accumulation toward a threshold. If that model is right, the early signal is not a decision that happens before awareness. The free-will question is not settled by either paper. Both are part of the record.
